picks.rationale: Hold premium QB allocation. Lamar and Ravens defensive leaders finished full practice without designations; do not assume a weakened Baltimore defense or a shootout. Buffalo tackle Spencer Brown remains questionable.

Hold rushing-role selection. Irving returned to full practice after rest; Gainwell is questionable after full Friday practice, so no vacated backfield work is assumed. Goedeke questionable and Egbuka out add offensive uncertainty.
Hold receiving/rushing participant at $6,300, preserving the earlier usage case. Brown is not on the current Bengals injury list; Perine competition and touchdown allocation remain uncertain.
Hold $6,000 allocation without an absence boost: St. Brown and Gibbs finished full practice without designations. Their presence preserves target competition.
Hold the price-sensitive receiving role, not a repeat of last week's efficiency. Prior retained 70% route share and Mitchell competition remain limitations; current report adds no Cooper restriction.
Hold receiving-role allocation. Lamar finished full practice all three days without a game designation, strengthening availability support without guaranteeing target share or effectiveness.
Hold low-cost TE involvement supported by prior retained 37 snaps/63%; broader 18 targets in five appearances and Cooper competition argue against projecting another two-touchdown result.

Hold the earlier target-participation case. Jenkins finished full practice, but Howard remains questionable after three DNPs and Pittsburgh's Watt/Highsmith have no designation; protection and absolute pass volume remain risks.

Replace Jets after Ossai/Sweat OUT and Bailey doubtful. Patriots front has DaQuan/Dre'Mont Jones full without designations; Miami tackle Proctor is OUT. Countercase: New England's zone/four-man-pressure problems meet an improving mobile Willis offense, with Davis/Elliss still questionable. No sack or point forecast asserted.

dispositions.decision: accept swap; partially accept interpretive correction
dispositions.reason: Hold Patriots DST. Claude correctly supplies both offense and defense splits; my earlier countercase should not imply Willis is strongest against zone. However, a weak offense versus a weak defense does not establish cancellation or a wash: EPA ranks and unlike conditional samples cannot simply be offset. The article itself has a prose/table tension about man/blitz weaknesses. Keep Miami recent improvement, run rate and New England zone pressure as counterevidence. Fresh market MIA18.25 versus LV22 supports the allocation but is not a sack or DK forecast.

Keep Cooper/Taylor and their $8,100 allocation. Shared passing environment can help both across a game, but a single normal Geno passing touchdown credits one receiver, not both; they compete for targets/TDs. No assumed Wilson rebound is evidence by itself. Retained routes and Taylor participation still support a price-sensitive hold; no newly verified better funding package established.

dispositions.decision: hold Concepcion; accept an investigation trigger, decline automatic substitution
dispositions.reason: Flournoy is verified WR/FLEX $4,600, ID44664785; exact other eight yield $49,900/$100. Pickens OUT before the actual freeze would justify reassessment, not prove Flournoy WR2/routes/targets. Newly inspected official Oct30 update confirms Pickens questionable, coach expects him to play, Turpin OUT; the generic report remains incomplete. If a pre-freeze official OUT and credible increased deployment evidence are observed, compare the legal alternative afresh; otherwise keep Concepcion. High Dallas implied total alone is insufficient. No conditional late swap after a valid freeze.

Agree a standalone swap costs $200 over cap. $4,500 Keenan for $4,700 Concepcion funds it exactly, but low team totals alone cannot determine the receiving-role downgrade and no supported overall improvement established. Retain Patriots; no forced budget churn.
